title: Working from home
paragraphs: If you go to work, you’re probably familiar with the routine of travelling to the office, hunting for an available desk, completing your tasks and then enduring your commute home. In many ways, it seems like an outdated working practice. And maybe that’s why more and more of us are now choosing to work from home.

There are, of course, many reasons for remote working, as it is also called. The demands of modern life and a desire for a better work-life balance has driven the trend, along with improved technology, which makes doing most tasks at home a doddle.

In the UK, figures from the Office for National Statistics show more than one and a half million people work from home for their main job. But, although logging on from the comfort of your sofa may appeal, especially if it’s part of a flexible working approach, some people are forced to work from home and find it hard going. Marketing consultant Mark Black told the BBC he struggled to switch off from work when he was based solely at home. He says: "I hated home working. You get up in the morning and stare at the same four walls, do your work, and try and clock off, but you can't." It’s true that being at home means you can’t physically leave your office behind, and as Emma Mamo from mental health charity Mind says: "Home workers don't always have the same opportunities to connect with people as their office-based colleagues.”

But remote working doesn’t always mean being at home. Cafes and workplace spaces offer a chance for workers, particularly self-employed people, to come together and interact with each other. There are also employees who have no choice but to work remotely because their companies have decided to do away with offices altogether to have a more agile workforce - it's certainly very cost effective and attractive for start-ups. But for those employed by businesses with a physical base, working at home provides a convenient alternative to the 9 to 5. And without the distraction of their colleagues, it can be the most productive place to work!

vocabulary.entry: remote working /rɪˈməʊt ˈwɜːkɪŋ/ 远程办公
vocabulary.example: Remote working has become a standard option in many industries.
vocabulary.translation: 远程办公已经成为许多行业的标准选项。

vocabulary.entry: work-life balance /ˌwɜːk laɪf ˈbæləns/ 工作与生活的平衡
vocabulary.example: Many people prioritize jobs that offer a good work-life balance.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人会优先选择那些能提供良好工作生活平衡的工作。

vocabulary.entry: doddle /ˈdɒdl/ n. 轻而易举的事
vocabulary.example: For an experienced programmer, this task is a doddle.
vocabulary.translation: 对有经验的程序员来说，这项任务简直小菜一碟。

vocabulary.entry: routine /ruːˈtiːn/ n. 日常惯例；例行公事
vocabulary.example: She likes to stick to her morning routine of jogging and reading.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢坚持自己早上慢跑加阅读的日常惯例。

vocabulary.entry: available /əˈveɪləbl/ adj. 可用的；可获得的
vocabulary.example: Is this conference room available for a meeting tomorrow?
vocabulary.translation: 这间会议室明天有空开会吗？

vocabulary.entry: outdated /ˌaʊtˈdeɪtɪd/ adj. 过时的；陈旧的
vocabulary.example: This software is outdated and no longer supported by the developer.
vocabulary.translation: 这款软件已经过时，开发商不再提供支持了。

vocabulary.entry: flexible working /ˈfleksəbl ˈwɜːkɪŋ/ 弹性工作
vocabulary.example: The company introduced flexible working to improve employee satisfaction.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司推出了弹性工作制来提高员工满意度。

vocabulary.entry: hard going /hɑːd ˈɡəʊɪŋ/ adj. 艰难的；难应付的
vocabulary.example: The first few weeks of the course were hard going, but it got easier later.
vocabulary.translation: 这门课刚开始的几周很难熬，但后来就变容易了。

vocabulary.entry: switch off /swɪtʃ ɒf/ 不再想着；不再关注（工作等）
vocabulary.example: It’s important to switch off from work when you’re on holiday.
vocabulary.translation: 度假的时候，放下工作不去想是很重要的。

vocabulary.entry: clock off /klɒk ɒf/ 打卡下班；结束工作
vocabulary.example: Most employees clock off at 6 pm in this company.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司的大多数员工下午6点下班。

vocabulary.entry: connect with /kəˈnekt wɪð/ 与……交流；与……建立联系
vocabulary.example: It’s easier to connect with colleagues in a face-to-face meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 面对面会议中，更容易和同事们交流沟通。

vocabulary.entry: self-employed /ˌself ɪmˈplɔɪd/ adj. 自主创业的；自由职业的
vocabulary.example: She’s self-employed and runs her own graphic design business.
vocabulary.translation: 她是自由职业者，经营着自己的平面设计工作室。

vocabulary.entry: interact /ˌɪntərˈækt/ v. 互动；交流
vocabulary.example: Children need to interact with their peers to develop social skills.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子需要和同龄人互动，才能培养社交能力。

vocabulary.entry: do away with /duː əˈweɪ wɪð/ 废除；取消
vocabulary.example: The school decided to do away with traditional exams and use projects instead.
vocabulary.translation: 这所学校决定废除传统考试，改用课题项目来评估学生。

vocabulary.entry: agile workforce /ˈædʒaɪl ˈwɜːkfɔːs/ 灵活的员工队伍
vocabulary.example: An agile workforce can adapt quickly to changes in the market.
vocabulary.translation: 灵活的员工队伍能快速适应市场的变化。

vocabulary.entry: cost effective /ˌkɒst ɪˈfektɪv/ adj. 性价比高的；划算的
vocabulary.example: Using energy-efficient bulbs is a cost effective way to reduce bills.
vocabulary.translation: 使用节能灯泡是降低账单开销的划算方法。

vocabulary.entry: start-up /ˈstɑːt ʌp/ n. 初创企业
vocabulary.example: The city has a lot of support programs for tech start-ups.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市有很多针对科技初创企业的扶持项目。

vocabulary.entry: physical base /ˈfɪzɪkl beɪs/ 实体办公地点
vocabulary.example: Although the team works remotely, the company still maintains a small physical base.
vocabulary.translation: 尽管团队远程办公，但这家公司仍保留了一个小型实体办公地点。

vocabulary.entry: alternative /ɔːlˈtɜːnətɪv/ n. 可供选择的事物
vocabulary.example: Cycling is a great alternative to driving for short trips.
vocabulary.translation: 短途出行时，骑自行车是开车之外的绝佳选择。

vocabulary.entry: 9 to 5 /ˌnaɪn tə ˈfaɪv/ 朝九晚五（的工作模式）
vocabulary.example: He’s tired of the 9 to 5 grind and wants to try freelance work.
vocabulary.translation: 他厌倦了朝九晚五的单调工作，想尝试自由职业。

vocabulary.entry: distraction /dɪˈstrækʃn/ n. 干扰；分心的事物
vocabulary.example: Turn off your phone to avoid distractions while studying.
vocabulary.translation: 学习时关掉手机，避免分心。

vocabulary.entry: productive /prəˈdʌktɪv/ adj. 高效的；多产的
vocabulary.example: A quiet environment helps me stay productive throughout the day.
vocabulary.translation: 安静的环境能让我一整天都保持高效的状态。

sentences.english: If you go to work, you’re probably familiar with the routine of travelling to the office, hunting for an available desk, completing your tasks and then enduring your commute home.
sentences.chinese: 如果你需要上班，或许对这样的日常很熟悉：奔波着去办公室，找一张空办公桌，完成手头的工作任务，然后再忍受通勤的疲惫回家。

sentences.english: In many ways, it seems like an outdated working practice.
sentences.chinese: 从很多方面来看，这都像是一种过时的工作模式。

sentences.english: And maybe that’s why more and more of us are now choosing to work from home.
sentences.chinese: 或许正因如此，如今越来越多的人选择居家办公。

sentences.english: There are, of course, many reasons for remote working, as it is also called.
sentences.chinese: 当然，这种也被称为“远程办公”的模式之所以兴起，有着诸多原因。

sentences.english: The demands of modern life and a desire for a better work-life balance has driven the trend, along with improved technology, which makes doing most tasks at home a doddle.
sentences.chinese: 现代生活的需求、人们对更好的工作生活平衡的渴望，再加上技术的进步，共同推动了这一趋势——技术的发展让在家完成大部分工作任务变得易如反掌。

sentences.english: In the UK, figures from the Office for National Statistics show more than one and a half million people work from home for their main job.
sentences.chinese: 英国国家统计局的数据显示，英国有超过150万人将居家办公作为自己的主业。

sentences.english: But, although logging on from the comfort of your sofa may appeal, especially if it’s part of a flexible working approach, some people are forced to work from home and find it hard going.
sentences.chinese: 不过，尽管窝在舒适的沙发上办公听起来很诱人——尤其是作为弹性工作模式的一部分——但有些人是被迫居家办公的，而且他们觉得这种模式很难熬。

sentences.english: Marketing consultant Mark Black told the BBC he struggled to switch off from work when he was based solely at home.
sentences.chinese: 市场营销顾问马克·布莱克告诉BBC，当他完全居家办公时，总是很难从工作状态中抽离出来。

sentences.english: You get up in the morning and stare at the same four walls, do your work, and try and clock off, but you can't."
sentences.chinese: 你早上起床，面对的是一成不变的四堵墙，处理完工作后，你试图下班，但根本做不到。”

sentences.english: It’s true that being at home means you can’t physically leave your office behind, and as Emma Mamo from mental health charity Mind says: "Home workers don't always have the same opportunities to connect with people as their office-based colleagues.”
sentences.chinese: 的确，居家办公意味着你无法真正“离开”办公室。心理健康慈善机构“心智”的艾玛·马莫也表示：“居家办公的员工，并不总能像办公室同事那样，拥有同等的人际交流机会。”

sentences.english: But remote working doesn’t always mean being at home.
sentences.chinese: 但远程办公并不等同于必须待在家里。

sentences.english: Cafes and workplace spaces offer a chance for workers, particularly self-employed people, to come together and interact with each other.
sentences.chinese: 咖啡馆和共享办公空间为职场人——尤其是自由职业者——提供了相聚交流的机会。

sentences.english: There are also employees who have no choice but to work remotely because their companies have decided to do away with offices altogether to have a more agile workforce - it's certainly very cost effective and attractive for start-ups.
sentences.chinese: 还有一些员工之所以不得不远程办公，是因为他们的公司为了打造更灵活的团队，决定彻底撤销实体办公室。这种模式无疑性价比很高，对初创企业来说颇具吸引力。

sentences.english: But for those employed by businesses with a physical base, working at home provides a convenient alternative to the 9 to 5.
sentences.chinese: 而对于那些受雇于有实体办公地点的公司的员工而言，居家办公是朝九晚五通勤模式之外的一种便捷选择。

sentences.english: And without the distraction of their colleagues, it can be the most productive place to work!
sentences.chinese: 而且没有了同事的干扰，家也能成为最高效的办公场所！
